questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the OSI model?

options.text: To provide a standardized framework for network communication.
To increase the speed of internet connections.
To define hardware specifications for computers.

questions.explanation: The OSI model provides a standardized framework for understanding and implementing network protocols, which is essential for communication between different systems.

distractorRationale.b: While the OSI model may help in optimizing communication, its primary purpose is not to increase speed.
distractorRationale.c: The OSI model does not define hardware specifications; it focuses on protocols.
distractorRationale.d: The OSI model does not replace TCP/IP; both models serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for ensuring reliable delivery of data?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer of the OSI model is responsible for ensuring reliable delivery of data, including error checking and flow control.

distractorRationale.a: The Network layer is responsible for routing data but does not ensure reliability.
distractorRationale.c: The Application layer deals with user interface and application-specific functions, not data delivery.
distractorRationale.d: The Session layer manages sessions but does not handle data reliability.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between TCP and UDP?

options.text: UDP guarantees delivery, while TCP does not.
TCP is connection-oriented, while UDP is connectionless.
UDP is used only for email communication.

questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and ensures reliable delivery of data, while UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery, making it faster but less reliable.

distractorRationale.a: TCP is not necessarily faster; in fact, it can be slower due to its reliability features.
distractorRationale.b: This statement is incorrect; TCP guarantees delivery, while UDP does not.
distractorRationale.d: UDP is not limited to email; it is used in various applications, including video streaming and online gaming.

questions.stem: The TCP/IP model has more layers than the OSI model.
questions.explanation: The TCP/IP model has fewer layers (four) compared to the OSI model (seven), making it simpler and more practical for implementation.
